name: GHRP-6

b.x: GHRP-6 (Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-6, CAS 87616-84-0) is a synthetic hexapeptide that binds the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) at the pituitary gland. In swine, its peak GH level was similar to ipamorelin's [10], but the trade-offs are real. Cabrales and colleagues characterized its pharmacokinetics in nine healthy male volunteers using IV administration [1], landing on a distribution half-life of 7.6 minutes and an elimination half-life around 2.5 hours. The commonly cited plasma half-life sits at roughly 20 minutes. What separates GHRP-6 from cleaner secretagogues like ipamorelin is its ghrelin mimicry. GHS-R1a is the ghrelin receptor, so agonism there doesn't just release GH. It also triggers orexigenic signaling that makes appetite spike within 20 minutes of injection. Cortisol and prolactin rise as well. In Bowers' study of 18 healthy men, both roughly doubled at 1 mcg/kg IV but not at lower doses [7]. Taken orally or intranasally, GHRP-6 left cortisol unchanged [2]. Community adoption across thousands of users on r/Peptides and bodybuilding forums has been consistent for over a decade. The top protocol pairs 100 mcg GHRP-6 with 100 mcg CJC-1295 No DAC (Mod GRF 1-29), injected two to three times daily on an empty stomach. Users report improved sleep, faster recovery, and lean mass accrual over 8 to 12 week cycles. No randomized controlled trials exist for body composition outcomes in healthy adults; the evidence base for performance use relies on GH-stimulation data extrapolated through community experience.

GHRP-6 binds the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHS-R1a) on pituitary somatotrophs. Lei and colleagues [3] showed that this binding stimulates phosphatidylinositol turnover, a calcium-dependent intracellular cascade that triggers growth hormone release from secretory granules. The result is a rapid, pulsatile GH spike detectable in serum within 15 to 30 minutes of subcutaneous injection. GHS-R1a is the endogenous ghrelin receptor. GHRP-6 mimics ghrelin's action at this site, which means it doesn't just release GH. It also activates orexigenic (appetite-stimulating) pathways through the hypothalamus. This dual action separates GHRP-6 from more selective GHRPs like ipamorelin, which produce GH pulses without the hunger surge. Beyond GH release, Berlanga-Acosta and colleagues described a separate receptor pathway through CD36. Their 2017 review [4] and subsequent 2024 cardioprotection study (PMC11169835) demonstrated cytoprotective effects in animal models, including wound healing acceleration [5] and cardiac protection against doxorubicin toxicity. These CD36-mediated effects operate independently of GH signaling. GHRP-6 also produces mild ACTH and cortisol elevation, along with a small prolactin increase. Bowers' group saw prolactin and cortisol about double at 1 mcg/kg IV [7]. Frieboes and colleagues found ACTH and cortisol rose after IV doses at night [6]; after oral or intranasal doses, cortisol stayed unchanged [2].
GHRP-6 benefits center on powerful GH secretion and appetite-driven mass gain.

- Produces a strong GH pulse. At 1 mcg/kg IV, peak GH reached about 69 µg/L in healthy men [7]. Community reports describe the GH and hunger effects within 15 to 30 minutes of injection. - Appetite stimulation through ghrelin receptor agonism hits within 20 minutes post-dose; hard gainers and bulking athletes treat this as a primary feature rather than a side effect. - Stacking with CJC-1295 No DAC (Mod GRF 1-29) produces complementary GH amplification because the two peptides act on different receptor pathways (GHS-R1a and GHRH receptor respectively). - Community users consistently report deeper sleep and faster recovery between training sessions, particularly with pre-bed dosing. - Cytoprotective properties shown in preclinical models, including wound healing acceleration [5] and cardioprotection via CD36 receptor binding [4], though these findings have not been confirmed in human performance contexts.

Dosing studied: 100–300 mcg per injection, 1–3×/day subcutaneous

Key Study

Limitations

No dose-ranging RCTs for performance/body-composition outcomes in healthy adults. Cytoprotection data is animal models only. Plasma levels fall fast after IV dosing (distribution half-life 7.6 min, elimination 2.5 h, PMID 23099431). Regulatory status (503B Category 2, 503A Category 3) limits clinical access.
Community Experience
Widely used for mass-gaining protocols due to intense appetite stimulation and strong GH pulse.
Community dosing: 100 mcg 3×/day (most common); 200–300 mcg for aggressive bulking
Often stacked with CJC-1295 No DAC as a GHRH/GHRP pair. Considered the best GHRP for bulking; appetite side effect is treated as a benefit.

Science confirms GHS-R1a agonism and acute GH release in humans. Community protocols extrapolate from mechanism to performance outcomes without RCT support. Appetite stimulation (ghrelin mimicry) is both scientifically validated and community-confirmed. Cycling rationale (receptor desensitization) is mechanistically plausible but not formally studied at community doses.
Community Community dosing consensus from peptide research communities

Your first GHRP-6 injection will probably teach you something about hunger you didn't know before. The appetite hit comes fast, usually within 20 minutes, and it's more intense than most people expect. Plan a meal. Reconstitution math for the standard 5 mg vial: add 2 mL bacteriostatic water. That gives you 2,500 mcg per mL, or 25 mcg per unit on a U-100 insulin syringe. So 100 mcg equals 4 units. 200 mcg equals 8 units. 300 mcg equals 12 units. The thing most beginners miss is the empty stomach requirement. Food within 30 minutes before or after injection substantially blunts the GH pulse. If you eat too close to your dose, you're wasting peptide. Time your injection 30 minutes before a planned meal so the hunger window works in your favor. Store reconstituted vials refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within four weeks. If you see particulates, color changes, or smell anything off after reconstitution, discard the vial.
GHRP-6 Cycle

Continuous GHS-R1a agonism by GHRP-6 leads to receptor downregulation and reduced pituitary sensitivity over time. This is the primary documented mechanism driving cycling protocols. Community reports consistent with mechanistic expectation: hunger response and GH-pulse symptoms typically diminish after 8–12 continuous weeks. A 4–8 week off period allows GHS-R1a density to recover. Antibody formation is theoretically possible with any exogenous peptide but has not been specifically reported as a clinical concern with GHRP-6 at community doses.
Reduced or absent hunger response post-injection (primary indicator)
Blunted tingling/flushing GH-pulse effects
Stalling sleep quality improvements
Plateaued or declining IGF-1 levels mid-cycle
Reconstitute a 5 mg vial with 2 mL bacteriostatic water Aim the stream against the glass wall, not directly onto the powder. Swirl gently until dissolved. This gives you 2,500 mcg per mL.
Draw your dose using a U-100 insulin syringe (29 to 31 gauge, 0.5 inch needle). For 100 mcg, draw to the 4-unit mark. For 200 mcg, draw to the 8-unit mark. For 300 mcg, draw to the 12-unit mark.
Pinch a fold of skin on your abdomen or outer thigh Insert the needle at a 45-degree angle into the subcutaneous fat layer. Inject slowly. Release the skin fold and withdraw.
Rotate injection sites with each dose to prevent lipodystrophy. Abdomen and outer thighs are the most common rotation areas.

Timing matters Inject on an empty stomach with no food 30 minutes before or after the injection. For pre-bed dosing, your last meal should be at least 30 minutes before the shot. For morning dosing, inject fasted and eat your first meal 30 minutes later.
If stacking with CJC-1295 No DAC (Mod GRF 1-29), you can draw both peptides into the same syringe and co-inject. Draw the CJC first, then the GHRP-6.
Refrigerate the reconstituted vial at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius after each use. Use within four weeks of reconstitution.

Works With
CJC-1295 No DAC (Mod GRF 1-29)
Gold-standard GHRH pairing. Acts on the GHRH receptor independently of GHS-R1a; community reports describe a larger GH pulse than either alone. Co-inject in same syringe on empty stomach.
100 mcg CJC-1295 No DAC + 100–200 mcg GHRP-6, 2–3×/day
Sermorelin
GHRH alternative to CJC-1295 No DAC. Shorter half-life (~12 min) but the same GHRH receptor pairing with GHRP-6. Some users prefer for milder, more physiologic GH pulse.
100–200 mcg sermorelin + 100 mcg GHRP-6, 1–2×/day pre-bed
CJC-1295 DAC
Long-acting GHRH (half-life ~6–8 days). Provides sustained background GHRH elevation while GHRP-6 generates pulsatile GH spikes. Less pulsatile than No DAC pairing: more blunted but convenient.
1–2 mg CJC-1295 DAC 2×/week + 100–200 mcg GHRP-6 2–3×/day
Avoid
Ipamorelin
Competes for the same GHS-R1a receptor. Co-administration provides no added GH benefit: one GHRP displaces the other. Choose one GHRP; stack it with a GHRH instead.
GHRP-2
Same GHS-R1a receptor competition: no added benefit from combining two GHRPs. If switching GHRPs mid-cycle for receptor variety, use sequentially, not simultaneously.
Hexarelin
GHS-R1a competitor. Combining adds nothing and may increase cortisol/prolactin burden without added GH benefit.
Somatostatin analogs (octreotide, lanreotide)
Directly antagonize GH release at the pituitary: will negate GHRP-6 GH-stimulating effect entirely.

The most serious concern with GHRP-6 is its effect on blood glucose regulation. Growth hormone directly opposes insulin action, and GHRP-6 compounds this problem by driving appetite-fueled caloric surpluses that can push fasting glucose upward. Anyone with uncontrolled diabetes, insulin resistance, or prediabetes should treat this as a hard contraindication. Fasting glucose monitoring every four weeks during a cycle isn't optional at this dosing level. Cortisol elevation is the second concern worth weighing carefully. GHRP-6 mildly raises ACTH and cortisol. Frieboes and colleagues saw both rise after four 50 mcg IV doses at night in healthy men [6]. Their 1999 follow-up found oral and intranasal GHRP-6 left cortisol unchanged [2]. At 100 mcg once daily, this is generally subclinical. Long-term cortisol data for GHRP-6 are lacking. In adults on hexarelin, a related GHRP, 16 weeks of twice-daily injections lowered the cortisol response [8]. At 200 to 300 mcg three times daily, watch for slower recovery, poorer sleep or stalled fat loss. Users running aggressive protocols should check morning cortisol at week four. Prolactin elevation also occurs, more so than with ipamorelin. At aggressive doses, some users report symptoms consistent with raised prolactin. Baseline and week-four prolactin checks are warranted if dosing exceeds 200 mcg per injection. Published side effects from the pharmacokinetic literature include tingling, facial flushing, dizziness, and transient warmth, all of which represent normal GH-pulse effects and typically resolve within 30 to 60 minutes. Community reports confirm these; they're predictable and dose-dependent. Water retention is common at higher doses (200 to 300 mcg range). Users report two to four pounds of water weight during peak dosing weeks. This resolves within one to two weeks of dose reduction or cessation. The appetite effect deserves its own warning. At 300 mcg, hunger becomes genuinely difficult to manage. This is a ghrelin mimetic doing exactly what ghrelin does. Users attempting to use GHRP-6 during a caloric deficit generally abandon the attempt; this peptide is a bulking tool. Injection site reactions (redness, mild irritation) are possible with any subcutaneous peptide. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are absolute contraindications. No human safety data exists for these populations.
Common Issues & Solutions

Hunger too intense to manage: Reduce to 50–75 mcg per injection, or restrict GHRP-6 use to pre-bed only. Hunger onset is ~20 min post-injection and peaks at ~45–60 min. Plan a high-calorie meal to follow; do not fast through the hunger window.

GH-pulse symptoms (tingling, dizziness, flushing) are severe: These are normal GH-pulse effects, typically resolving within 30–60 min. If persistent or severe, reduce dose by 50% and titrate up more slowly. Sitting during injection and for 15 min after reduces dizziness.

Diminishing response after 6–8 weeks (no hunger, no sleep improvement, no pump): GHS-R1a desensitization. Cycle off for 4–6 weeks. Adding a GHRH (CJC-1295 No DAC) may partially compensate but will not fully reverse desensitization: an off-cycle break is required.

Water retention is notable: At 300 mcg doses water retention can be significant. Reduce to 100–200 mcg, ensure adequate hydration and moderate sodium intake. Water retention typically resolves within 1–2 weeks of dose reduction or cessation.

No results despite following protocol: Verify (1) injections are on an empty stomach: food within 30 min substantially blunts GH pulse; (2) reconstitution math is correct (5 mg vial + 2 mL bac water = 4 units per 100 mcg on U-100 syringe); (3) peptide stored properly: refrigerated post-reconstitution, used within 4 weeks.

GHRP-6 is not FDA-approved for any medical indication. It is classified as a research chemical in the United States. On September 29, 2023, FDA placed GHRP-6 in 503B Category 2, citing immunogenicity risk and possible effects on cortisol and blood glucose. It is not on the 503A bulks list (21 CFR 216.23), and FDA's 503A list (updated May 14, 2026) places it in Category 3. All GHRP-6 currently available is unregulated research-grade product. For athletes, GHRP-6 is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) under the category of growth hormone secretagogues. It is banned both in-competition and out-of-competition. Regulatory status varies by country. GHRP-6 is sold online labeled "for research purposes only." This content is provided for educational and informational purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a qualified healthcare provider before using any peptide or research compound.

faqs.q: What is the recommended GHRP-6 dosage?
faqs.a: Beginner: 100 mcg subcutaneous, 2-3 times daily. Moderate: 200 mcg per injection. Aggressive: 300 mcg per injection. Best results come from dosing on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before food. Most users inject before bed and upon waking.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of GHRP-6?
faqs.a: Intense hunger is the hallmark side effect. GHRP-6 spikes ghrelin signaling more aggressively than ipamorelin or GHRP-2. Water retention, joint stiffness, and mild cortisol elevation are also reported. Numbness or tingling in extremities can occur at higher doses. Blood glucose may rise with prolonged use.

faqs.q: How does GHRP-6 differ from ipamorelin?
faqs.a: Both stimulate GH release through the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a), but GHRP-6 also raises cortisol and prolactin. Ipamorelin is selective for GH only. No human study has compared their GH peaks. In swine, peak GH reached 74 ng/ml with GHRP-6 and 65 with ipamorelin, which the authors called very similar (PMID 9849822). GHRP-6 carries more side effects. Community preference has shifted toward ipamorelin for cleaner GH stimulation.

Add 2 mL bacteriostatic water to a 5 mg vial. That gives 2,500 mcg/mL, or 25 mcg per unit on a 100-unit insulin syringe. For 100 mcg, draw 4 units. For 200 mcg, draw 8 units. Store reconstituted vial refrigerated at 2-8 degrees C and use within 3-4 weeks.

Yes. Continuous GHS-R1a agonism leads to receptor downregulation after 8-12 weeks. The standard community cycle is 8-12 weeks on, 4-8 weeks off. Signs of desensitization include reduced hunger response post-injection and blunted GH-pulse symptoms like tingling or flushing.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of GHRP-6?
faqs.a: The half-life of GHRP-6 is 7.6 min distribution, 2.5 h elimination (IV). This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.
